newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook--Platinum to call tune for bullion.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook--Platinum to call tune for bullion.

text.p: Platinum and palladium, which led the precious metals sector for the past week, are forecast to continue calling the tune for gold prices this week.
But analysts warned that after a week of dramatic rises, which ended in a sharp reversal as speculators took their profits, prices might prove more volatile.
"Platinum's rise has been vertical and that cannot be sustained," said Elli Gifford, technical analyst at Investment Research of Cambridge.
Platinum topped $406.00 per ounce on Friday for the first time since May last year and its sister metal palladium fixed at $157.00 on Thursday, its highest fixing since July 1995.
Gold's performance was sluggish in comparison but it did get as far as $360.60 on Friday, its highest fix since January 3 this year.

Bullion's chance of accelerating this week were diminished by the higher price restraining the rush for small gold bars coveted by traditional gold affinity hoarders in the Middle and Far East that had supported gold at lower levels.
Dealers said concerns over the non-appearance of Russian exports of platinum and palladium so far this year were fuelling demand for these metals, especially in Japan, their largest consumer.
A twist was added to the Russia-Japan problem at the weekend when workers at Russia's huge Norilsk mining and processing plant voted to strike in mid-March over unpaid wages.
However, dealers said the strike issue was already factored into the price.
Workers at the cash-strapped plant in Arctic Siberia were last paid in full in October.
Russia is the leading producer of palladium and the second largest exporter of platinum after South Africa and its internal problems added to the need to stock up on the platinum group metals.
"There is still no sign of Russia opening trade talks with Japan. It all depends on them now," one dealer said.
Changes to Russia's exporting administration and delays in passing the 1997 budget postponed the start of negotiations with Japanese importers and consequently exports.
"There are a lot of problems in Russia and although people will take profits out, the market will continue to firm until Russia and Japan sit down to talk," the dealer said.
Gifford noted that all the target prices on the charts had been fulfilled so far and the next thing could be a challenge of the Spring 1996 high of $407.00.
"I can't talk it up much higher than that," she said.
Cliff Green, a chartist at Trend Analysis, warned against misjudging the moves in the precious metals markets.

"People may think this is the beginning of a major bull market but I am sure it is not. It is a correction and when it is over prices could fall sharply," he said, adding that very volatile prices were likely this week.
Platinum is used in jewellery, electronics, many chemical industry applications and in autocatalysts to remove toxic gases from car exhaust fumes.
Palladium is also used in catalytic converters, electronics and chemicals and as major constituent in dental alloys.
Annual production of both metals is small compared with gold and essentially limited to Russia and South Africa.
According to leading refiner Johnson Matthey, platinum production totalled 4.98 million ounces in 1995, of which 3.37 million ounces were from South Africa and 1.28 million ounces from Russia.
Palladium availability totalled 6.34 million ounces, of which 4.20 million came from Russia, about half of which was from the government stockpile, and 1.6 million from South Africa.
Reflecting the impact of losing its Russian supplies, Japan imports of platinum and palladium from the dealer market surged in January, according to Finance Ministry statistics issued last Friday.
Palladium imports jumped 224 percent compared with January 1995 to 8.15 tonnes and platinum purchases were up 63.6 percent to 7.1 tonnes compared with the previous year.

"Because we expected Japan-Russia platinum group metal export talks to be delayed we have stepped up our spot market buying since the end of last year," an official at a major Japanese bullion house said.
